description: Polygons of the seafloor searched by the ATSB-led MH370 underwater search (Oct 2014 - Jan 2017) derived from Geoscience Australia public data; plus the 2014 Bluefin-21 area and the 2014 wide area for context. Coordinates are [lon, lat] WGS84, closed rings, counter-clockwise exteriors.
atsb_published_area_km2: 'in excess of 120,000' (ATSB 2017 p. i); 'more than 120,000 ... searched and eliminated with a high degree of confidence' (p. ii); 'in the order of 120,000' (p. 63)

atsb_detection_confidence.high_confidence_coverage: >95% confidence of detection; 97.4% of combined area
atsb_detection_confidence.source: ATSB, The Operational Search for MH370, 3 Oct 2017, pp. 95-96 (Figure 73)

validation_tilecache_z8_vs_union_km2.note: zoom-8 tiles have ~0.5 km pixels, so edges are inflated/deflated by ~1 tile pixel

polygons.name: ATSB underwater search 2014-2017: sonar coverage envelope (all sensors, interior gaps filled)
polygons.source: Geoscience Australia / AusSeabed, 'The Search for Flight MH370 - Phase 2 5 m resolution sonar images' (GA eCat 120969, doi:10.4225/25/5b0cd3b139def), CC BY 4.0; WFS layer ausseabed:MH370_Phase_2_Sonar_Imagery_Backscatter_Inverse_Deep_Tow__SSS__5m_2018_L0_Coverage and WMS layers for AUV SSS, Go Phoenix SAS, Dong Hai Jiu 101 SAS at https://warehouse.ausseabed.gov.au/geoserver/ows (retrieved 2026-11-05)
polygons.method_detail: Union of GA per-sensor Phase 2 sonar coverage (deep-tow SSS from GA WFS vector coverage; AUV SSS, Go Phoenix SAS, DHJ101 SAS from GA WMS alpha masks rendered at 0.002 deg), largest connected component, interior holes filled, vectorised by marching squares and Douglas-Peucker simplified with 0.005 deg tolerance.
polygons.notes: Represents seafloor imaged by sonar, which is what the ATSB counted as 'searched' (~120,000 km2). Interior data holidays visible at 0.2 km resolution total only 14.49 km2 and are listed separately (kind=data_gap). ATSB states 0.5% data gaps (0% detection) and 2.1% lower-probability-of-detection areas (50-90%, nominal 70%) by a 100 m x 100 m metric; most are smaller than 200 m x 200 m and cannot be located from public rasters. Error budget: simplification Hausdorff <= 0.449 km, raster pixel 0.18 x 0.22 km, sonar positioning ~0.05 km (ATSB p.55). Thin outlying strips not connected to the main area (5.25 km2) are excluded.

polygons.name: ATSB confidence area 'red' (Figure 73) within the searched envelope
polygons.source: Geoscience Australia / AusSeabed, 'The Search for Flight MH370 - Phase 2 5 m resolution sonar images' (GA eCat 120969, doi:10.4225/25/5b0cd3b139def), CC BY 4.0; WFS layer ausseabed:MH370_Phase_2_Sonar_Imagery_Backscatter_Inverse_Deep_Tow__SSS__5m_2018_L0_Coverage and WMS layers for AUV SSS, Go Phoenix SAS, Dong Hai Jiu 101 SAS at https://warehouse.ausseabed.gov.au/geoserver/ows (retrieved 2026-11-05); area definitions and statistics: ATSB, The Operational Search for MH370 (2017), pp. 95-96, Figure 73
polygons.method_detail: Envelope pixels classified by foot-point latitude on, and signed perpendicular distance from, the GA/ATSB 7th arc drawn at 40,000 ft (GA feature service 7thArc_SingleLine). Along-arc cuts at -36.09 S and -34.64 S where the public coverage width changes; across-arc split of the southern block at 27.5 NM NW / 25 NM SE (ATSB text). Parts >= 2 km2, 0.005 deg simplification.
polygons.atsb_definition: 'Indicative Search Area' out to 27.5 NM NW and 25 NM SE of the 7th arc; deep-tow SSS, SAS and AUV infill
polygons.notes: Boundaries between areas are inferred (along-arc cut uncertainty ~+/-0.06 deg latitude, ~5-7 km; the outer edges are the coverage envelope, error ~0.5 km). The ATSB figure shows these areas as outlined polygons; our reconstruction reproduces the ATSB combined statistics when area-weighted (see summary.atsb_fig73_regions_weighted_check).

polygons.notes: To define the wide area representing high confidence in localising the aircraft, the ATSB search area definition report (published 26 June 2014) used a distance of 100 nautical miles behind the 7th arc and 100 nautical miles forward of the arc.
